title: Episodic Impairment of Consciousness, Falls and Drop Attacks
scope: Source-grounded diagnostic decision support; not a validated diagnostic score

implementation.navigation: Select an option and follow its next node ID

history: skin color, sweating, pulse and respiration
post-event confusion and time to recovery
cardiac, vascular, neurologic and medication history
examination: gait, balance, strength, sensation, reflexes and eye movements
initial_assessment.safety_note: Urgent evaluation for severe injury, ongoing altered consciousness, concerning cardiac symptoms, new focal neurological deficits or other acute instability; this safety overlay is an implementation precaution, not a quoted Bradley decision rule.

clinical_cautions: Historical text uses complex partial seizure and pseudoseizure; modern labels are focal impaired-awareness seizure and functional/psychogenic nonepileptic seizure.
Do not treat historical frequency comparisons or single clinical signs as validated likelihood ratios.
A normal routine EEG does not exclude epilepsy; event-correlated video-EEG is important for uncertain spells.
Convulsive movements and incontinence can occur in syncope.
Avoid unsupervised carotid sinus massage; source itself describes cerebrovascular risks.
The source uses an older orthostatic blood-pressure threshold and includes dated investigations/treatments; current standards must be checked before clinical deployment.
This is a diagnostic routing algorithm, not a definitive diagnosis or treatment protocol.
